mainTopic: משה's doubt about בנות צלפחד and ownership of ארץ ישראל, honoring a student before his teacher, and the three praises of בנות צלפחד
overview: This amud finishes רבי שמעון השקמוני's teaching that good things come about through worthy people, which is why the inheritance laws came through בנות צלפחד. The גמרא then asks: if ארץ ישראל already counted as owned by those who left מצרים, what was משה unsure about? It answers that this was exactly his doubt, from the word 'מורשה'. The resolution is that both readings are true, and the song at the sea ('תביאמו', 'bring THEM') supports this. Next, the גמרא asks why the daughters would go to the נשיאים after משה. רבי יאשיה reverses the order of the פסוק. אבא חנן says everyone sat together in the בית המדרש. Their argument turns on whether a student may be honored in his teacher's presence, and the הלכה depends on whether the teacher himself honors the student. Finally, a ברייתא praises בנות צלפחד as wise, skilled interpreters, and righteous. The גמרא explains each praise, and since they married at forty, it says a miracle let them have children, like יוכבד.

steps.title: Good things come through good people
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי שמעון השקמוני's teaching: merit is brought about through the meritorious and liability through the guilty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because good things are brought about through a worthy person, and bad things through a guilty person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that started on the previous page. It explains why the laws of inheritance came through בנות צלפחד and the punishment law came through the מקושש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those laws could have been written in the תורה without any story. But הקב"ה arranges that a good law is taught through worthy people, so בנות צלפחד earned it. A punishment law is taught through someone who sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: bring about, cause to roll toward

steps.whatToRemember: זכות comes through the זכאי and חובה through the חייב. בנות צלפחד earned having the inheritance laws taught through them.

phrases.english: that merit is brought about through one who is worthy,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page, about why the inheritance laws came through בנות צלפחד.

phrases.english: and liability through one who is guilty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the teaching of רבי שמעון השקמוני, which began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Merit is brought about through the meritorious and liability through the guilty.

steps.title: If the land was already owned, what was משה unsure about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that ארץ ישראל was already considered owned: if so, משה should have had no doubt about the double portion of בנות צלפחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that ארץ ישראל was already considered owned, what was משה unsure about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. If ארץ ישראל already counted as owned by those who left מצרים, משה's question about בנות צלפחד makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the land was already owned, then חפר owned his share. צלפחד was a בכור, so he would get a double portion, and his daughters would inherit it. That seems obvious, so why did משה need to ask?

keyTerms.meaning: and if it enters your mind (if you think that)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that ארץ ישראל was already held in their possession,
phrases.notes: He means owned by the generation that left מצרים, even before they came in and divided it.

phrases.english: what was he unsure about?
phrases.notes: 'He' is משה, who brought the question of בנות צלפחד before הקב"ה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּחְזֶקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the story of בנות צלפחד to challenge the view that the land was already owned.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that ארץ ישראל was considered owned by the generation of יציאת מצרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the land was already owned, the daughters' claim to the בכור's double portion would be obvious. So משה's doubt shows the land was not yet owned.

steps.title: משה's doubt was this very question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that משה was unsure about exactly this: does 'מורשה' mean the land is an inheritance from the fathers, or that this generation only passes it on but does not inherit it?
steps.simpleTranslation: That itself is what he was unsure about, as it says: 'And I will give it to you as a מורשה, I am ה׳.' Does it mean it is an inheritance for you from your fathers? Or perhaps it means they pass it on but do not inherit it themselves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. משה's doubt was not about the daughters' rights directly. He was unsure whether the land counted as already owned at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מורשה can be read two ways. Read as ירושה, it means the land comes to you from your fathers, so you already own it. Read as מורישין, it means this generation only passes it on to their children, because they will die in the מדבר.

keyTerms.meaning: they pass on, give as an inheritance

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse מורישין (they pass it on to others) with יורשין (they receive it themselves). The whole doubt depends on the difference.

phrases.english: That itself is what he was unsure about,
as it is written: 'And I will give it to you
as a heritage, I am ה׳.'
Does it mean it is an inheritance for you from your fathers?
Or perhaps it means that they pass it on but do not inherit it themselves?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by saying משה's doubt was about whether the land was owned at all.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the doubt: the question itself was about ownership of the land.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה's doubt shows the land was clearly not considered owned.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה's doubt came from two possible readings of מורשה. One reading means the land was owned, the other means it was not.

steps.title: Both readings are true
steps.stepSummary: משה's question was resolved: both meanings are correct. The land is an inheritance from the fathers, and that generation passes it on without entering it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they resolved it for him: both. It is an inheritance for you from your fathers, and they pass it on but do not inherit it themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the resolution of משה's doubt. Both readings of מורשה are correct together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The land counts as owned through the fathers, so the בכור's double portion applies and בנות צלפחד receive it. At the same time, the people who left מצרים would not enter the land themselves. They only pass it on to their children.
steps.whatToRemember: Both are true: the land is a ירושה from the fathers, and that generation are מורישין ואינן יורשין.

phrases.english: And they resolved it for him: both are true.
phrases.notes: The answer came from Heaven, since משה brought the question before ה׳.

phrases.english: It is an inheritance for you from your fathers,
and they pass it on but do not inherit it themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the two-sided doubt raised in the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both readings of מורשה are correct together.

steps.title: 'You will bring THEM': an unknowing prophecy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the idea that that generation would not enter the land. At the sea they sang 'תביאמו' (bring them) instead of 'תביאנו' (bring us).
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'You will bring them and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance.' It does not say 'bring us' but 'bring them.' This teaches that they were prophesying without knowing what they were prophesying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from the song at the sea. It supports the idea that the generation leaving מצרים would not enter the land themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people singing were the ones who left מצרים, yet they said 'bring THEM', not 'bring US'. Without realizing it, they were prophesying that only their children would enter. This backs up מורישין ואינן יורשין.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written

steps.whatToRemember: 'תביאמו' and not 'תביאנו' shows that the generation of the sea unknowingly prophesied they would not enter the land.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
'You will bring them and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance.'
phrases.notes: שמות 15:17, from the song at the sea.

phrases.english: It does not say 'You will bring us,' but 'You will bring them.'
This teaches that they were prophesying,
but they did not know what they were prophesying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to support the second half of the resolution.
steps.raayaObject: That the generation of יציאת מצרים would pass on the land but not enter it themselves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 15:17, which says 'תביאמו' (bring them) and not 'תביאנו' (bring us).

steps.title: Why would they go to the princes after משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק listing משה, אלעזר הכהן, the נשיאים and the congregation. It asks how it makes sense that בנות צלפחד went to lesser people after משה gave no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the daughters stood before משה, then אלעזר, then the princes and the whole congregation. Could it be that משה had no answer for them, and then they went to ask the princes and the congregation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about בנות צלפחד and points out that its order seems impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read in order, the פסוק sounds like the daughters asked משה first and then went down the ladder to lesser people. That makes no sense. If משה, the greatest teacher, did not know the answer, the נשיאים and the congregation certainly would not know it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible? (used here as a challenge)

phrases.english: "And they stood before Moses,
and before Elazar the priest,
and before the princes and all the congregation" –
is it possible that they stood before Moses, etc.,
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of the list, meaning אלעזר too.

phrases.english: and they said nothing to them,
and then they stood before the princes and all the congregation?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of בנות צלפחד, now looking at the פסוק describing how they came forward.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain order of the list in במדבר 27:2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lesser people could not answer a question that משה himself could not answer, so asking them afterward is illogical.

steps.title: Read the verse in reverse order
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה answers that the list should be read backwards. The daughters started with the congregation and worked their way up to משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, flip the order of the פסוק and learn it that way. This is the view of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה answers the question by telling us to read the פסוק's list in reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we reverse the order, the daughters went up step by step, from the congregation to the נשיאים to אלעזר and finally to משה. Each group could not answer, so they went higher. This removes the problem of asking lesser people after משה.

keyTerms.meaning: Flip around the order of the פסוק

phrases.english: Rather, reverse the order of the verse and expound it,
these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the order of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The daughters went from משה down to lesser people.
steps.terutzMaskana: They went from the lesser people up to משה.

steps.title: Everyone was sitting together in the study hall
steps.stepSummary: אבא חנן, quoting רבי אליעזר, gives a different answer. All the people listed were sitting together in the בית המדרש, and the daughters stood before all of them at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא חנן said in the name of רבי אליעזר: they were all sitting in the בית המדרש, and the daughters went and stood before all of them together.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer is given: there was no order of asking at all, because everyone was in one room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view the daughters did not go from group to group. They stood once before everyone. The פסוק simply lists the people who were present, from the most important down.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Abba Chanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
They were sitting in the study hall,
and the daughters went and stood before all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא חָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same challenge from step 6, competing with רבי יאשיה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the scene so that there is no order of asking
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The daughters went to each group separately, one after another.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone was present at once, and the list just names who was there.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the different answers of רבי יאשיה and אבא חנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by asking what deeper idea causes the two opinions to differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers solve the problem, so the גמרא wants to know why רבי יאשיה did not simply say everyone was together. The answer will show a disagreement about honor.

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the split between steps 7 and 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates רבי יאשיה from אבא חנן.

steps.title: Honoring a student in front of his teacher
steps.stepSummary: One view holds that we may honor a student in the presence of his teacher, and the other holds that we may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that we give honor to a student in the presence of his teacher. The other master holds that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions disagree about whether a student may be honored while his teacher is present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא חנן holds that honor may be given. So the פסוק could list the נשיאים and the congregation even though משה was there. רבי יאשיה holds that it may not, so if משה had been present, nobody else would be mentioned. That is why he must say the daughters went to each group at a different time.

keyTerms.meaning: In the presence of the teacher

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say which name goes with which side. The one who allows honor is אבא חנן, and the one who forbids it is רבי יאשיה.

phrases.english: One master holds:
phrases.notes: This is אבא חנן, who has everyone sitting together and still listed.

phrases.english: we show honor to a student in the presence of the teacher,
and the other master holds: we do not show honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is whether honor may be shown to a student in his teacher's presence.

steps.title: Two rulings stated on the same question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא records two halachic rulings. One says we may honor the student, and the other says we may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is that we give honor, and the הלכה is that we do not give honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states two rulings that seem to point in opposite directions. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions from step 10 are recorded as הלכה. On the surface that is impossible, and the גמרא is about to point this out.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: we show honor,
and the halakha is: we do not show honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives practical rulings on the disagreement explained in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both positions are recorded as הלכה, which needs to be reconciled.

steps.title: The two rulings contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that one ruling contradicts the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: One הלכה contradicts the other הלכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two rulings cannot both be true as stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot rule both that honor is given and that it is not given, unless they apply to different situations.

keyTerms.meaning: One ruling contradicts the other ruling

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: one halakha contradicts the other halakha!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two rulings of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two opposite rulings in step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opposite rulings on the same question cannot both stand.

steps.title: It depends on whether the teacher honors the student
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. Honor is given to the student when his own teacher honors him, and not when his teacher does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rulings do not really contradict. One applies where the teacher himself honors the student, so others may honor him too. The other applies where the teacher does not honor him, so others may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each ruling applies to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is the teacher's own behavior. If the teacher shows the student respect, others may do the same in his presence. If the teacher does not, honoring the student in front of him is not allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether we may honor a student in his teacher's presence depends on the teacher. If the teacher honors the student, we may honor him too. If not, we may not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule for showing respect to students and teachers. It also shows the standard way the גמרא resolves two rulings that seem to clash: each one applies to a different case.

phrases.english: The contradiction between one halakha and the other is not difficult:
this ruling applies where his teacher gives him honor,

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּלָא פְּלִיג לֵיהּ רַבֵּיהּ יְקָרָא.
phrases.english: and that ruling applies where his teacher does not give him honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings cover the same situation and clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: One ruling applies where the teacher honors the student, and the other where he does not.

steps.title: The three praises of בנות צלפחד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that בנות צלפחד were wise, skilled interpreters of פסוקים, and righteous.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the daughters of צלפחד were wise, they were interpreters of verses, and they were righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא with three praises of בנות צלפחד. This sets up the next steps, which will explain each praise one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three separate qualities without giving proof. Each one is a heading. The גמרא will now show where each quality appears in the story of how they asked for their father's נחלה.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughters of צלפחד, who asked משה for their father's inheritance
Women skilled at drawing lessons from פסוקים

phrases.english: It was taught: the daughters of Zelophehad
are wise,
are interpreters of verses,
are righteous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of honoring a student in front of his teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בנות צלפחד had three praiseworthy qualities: wisdom, skill in reading פסוקים, and righteousness.

steps.title: They were wise because they spoke at the right moment
steps.stepSummary: The first praise, 'wise', is explained: they raised their claim at exactly the right time.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were wise, because they spoke in a way that fit the moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first praise. Their wisdom showed in their timing. This sets up the story that comes next as the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wisdom here is not general intelligence. It means knowing when to speak. The next step shows what was happening at that moment that made it the perfect time.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the moment, at the right time

phrases.english: They are wise —
for they spoke according to the moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the three praises listed in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Their wisdom was in choosing the right moment to present their claim.

steps.title: Proof: they spoke up while משה taught about יבום
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק relates that משה was teaching the laws of יבום, and the daughters used that moment to show that either they inherit or their mother needs יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: משה רבינו was sitting and teaching the section about יבום, as it says, 'If brothers dwell together.' They said to him: If we count like a son, give us an inheritance like a son. If not, our mother should go through יבום! Right away, 'And משה brought their case before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the 'right moment' idea with a teaching of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק. The daughters spoke while משה was teaching about יבום and used that law to build their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום applies only when a man dies with no children. The daughters argued: if daughters count as children, we should inherit. If they don't count, our father died childless, so our mother needs יבום. Since the הלכה could not have it both ways, משה immediately brought the question to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah section about יבום (a widow of a childless man marrying his brother)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said:
This teaches that Moses our teacher was
sitting and teaching the section about levirate marriage,
as it is stated: “If brothers dwell together.”

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כְּבֵן אָנוּ חֲשׁוּבִין –
phrases.english: They said to him: If we are considered like a son,
give us an inheritance like a son;
if not, our mother should enter levirate marriage!
phrases.notes: If daughters don't count as children, then their father died childless, and that is exactly when יבום applies.

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד – ״וַיַּקְרֵב מֹשֶׁה אֶת מִשְׁפָּטָן לִפְנֵי ה׳״.
phrases.english: Immediately: “And Moses brought their case before the Lord.”

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source showing why their timing was wise.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that they spoke at the right moment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק's teaching that משה was teaching the laws of יבום when they came.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how they tied their claim to the law being taught at that moment, which forced an immediate decision.

steps.title: They were interpreters: 'If he had a son, we would not have spoken'
steps.stepSummary: The second praise is explained: they understood that daughters inherit only when there is no son.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were interpreters of verses, because they said: If our father had a son, we would not have spoken up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second praise. They showed they understood the law precisely: their claim existed only because their father had no son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They did not claim that daughters always share with sons. They limited their claim to a case with no son. This careful understanding of how inheritance works is what makes them 'interpreters'.

keyTerms.meaning: If (in a case that did not happen)

phrases.english: They are interpreters — for they would say:

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ הָיָה לוֹ בֵּן, לֹא דִּבַּרְנוּ.
phrases.english: If he had had a son, we would not have spoken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first praise to the second praise from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They understood that daughters inherit only when there is no son.

steps.title: A ברייתא says 'daughter' instead of 'son'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with a ברייתא that has them saying 'if he had a daughter'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא says 'daughter'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects. Another ברייתא quotes the sisters as saying 'if he had a daughter, we would not have spoken.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: That wording makes no sense. They were themselves daughters, so their father obviously had daughters. The גמרא needs to explain the strange wording.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But it is taught: “Daughter”!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא has them saying 'if he had a daughter', which is odd because they were daughters themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The quote 'if he had a son, we would not have spoken.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says 'daughter', which contradicts the quote and makes no sense on its own terms.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: remove the word 'daughter'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the word 'daughter' should be removed from that ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Take out the word 'daughter' from here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers by fixing the ברייתא. The word 'daughter' should simply be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He treats the word as a mistake in the wording. Once it is removed, the ברייתא matches the quote about a son.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Remove from here “daughter.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'daughter' does not belong there.

steps.title: אביי: 'daughter' means a son's daughter
steps.stepSummary: אביי keeps the word and explains it: even if there had been a son's daughter, they would not have spoken.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even if there had been a daughter of a son, we would not have spoken.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer. He keeps the word 'daughter' and explains that it means a son's daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son's daughter takes her father's place and inherits before the dead man's own daughters. So the sisters were saying they knew even a granddaughter through a son would come first. This shows even sharper understanding, and no word needs to be removed.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'interpreters' praise has two readings: רבי ירמיה removes 'daughter' from the ברייתא, while אביי reads it as 'a son's daughter', who would also inherit before them.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even if there had been a daughter of a son,
we would not have spoken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ הָיָה בַּת לַבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 18, different from רבי ירמיה's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording without changing it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Daughter' means a daughter of צלפחד himself, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Daughter' means a son's daughter, who would inherit before them.

steps.title: They were righteous: they married only fitting men
steps.stepSummary: The third praise is explained: they married only men who were right for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were righteous, because they married only men who were fitting for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third praise. Their righteousness showed in being careful about whom they married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They did not rush into marriage. They waited for husbands who were truly suitable, and that self-control is counted as righteousness.

phrases.english: They are righteous —
for they married only those fitting for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion about 'daughter' to the third praise from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Their righteousness was that they married only suitable husbands.

steps.title: Even the youngest married at forty or older
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds that even the youngest sister was at least forty when she married.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught: Even the youngest of them did not marry at less than forty years old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a teaching from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. It shows how long they waited for the right husbands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up the third praise. Even the youngest waited until forty, which shows how firmly they held out for a fitting match.
steps.whatToRemember: The three praises of בנות צלפחד: wise because of their timing, interpreters because they understood the order of inheritance, righteous because they waited for fitting husbands.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov taught:
Even the youngest among them
did not marry at less than forty years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail that supports the third praise in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the youngest daughter married no younger than forty.

steps.title: How could women who married at forty have children?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר בן יעקב using רב חסדא's rule that a woman who marries at forty can no longer give birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? רב חסדא said: if a woman marries before twenty, she can give birth until sixty. If she marries at twenty, she can give birth until forty. If she marries at forty, she can no longer give birth at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the claim that the daughters of צלפחד married at forty or older. It uses a rule from רב חסדא about when women can have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule says a woman who first marries at forty cannot have children. The daughters of צלפחד did have children, so how could they have married that late? The גמרא sees a clash between the two statements.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a word that opens a challenge)
But didn't he say...? (brings a source against the claim)
She can no longer give birth

phrases.english: Is that so? But doesn't Rav Ḥisda say:
If she married when younger than twenty,
she can give birth until sixty;
if she married at twenty, she can give birth until forty;
if she married at forty, she can no longer give birth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's claim in step 22 that the youngest daughter was at least forty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the daughters of צלפחד married at forty or older
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא says a woman who marries at forty cannot give birth, yet these women had children.

steps.title: A miracle happened for them, like for יוכבד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that because they were righteous, a miracle let them have children, just like יוכבד, and starts bringing a פסוק to show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because they were righteous women, a miracle was done for them, like for יוכבד. As it is written: 'And a man from the house of לוי went, and took a daughter of לוי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the claim that they married at forty and explains that a miracle let them have children. It compares them to יוכבד and begins quoting a פסוק, which it explains on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule is not rejected; it describes the normal way of the world. These women were an exception because of their righteousness. The comparison to יוכבד shows that such a miracle already happened before.

keyTerms.meaning: A miracle was done for them
Mother of משה, אהרן and מרים

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא can keep a general rule of nature and still explain an unusual case as a miracle, without dropping either statement.

phrases.english: Rather, since they are righteous women,
a miracle was done for them, like for Jochebed,
as it is written: “And a man of the house of Levi went,
and took a daughter of Levi”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב חסדא in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exceptional case: a miracle beyond the normal rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Women who marry at forty cannot have children, so the daughters of צלפחד could not have married that late.
steps.terutzMaskana: They did marry at forty, but because of their righteousness a miracle let them have children, as with יוכבד.
